html: † נִדְבָּךְ n.m. row or layer, course (𝔗 NH id.; NH also מִדְבָּךְ id. (LevyNHWB iii. 23), cf. مِدْمَاكٌ as loan-word Frä12; borrowed from Assyrian nadbaku, mountain-slope according to DlPr 150 (cf. BaZA ii. 115 f. HptGN 1883, 96; BASi. 8. 15), but meaning not very suitable NöZMG xl (1886), 733 MeyEntst. J. 46);—abs. נ׳ Ezr 6:4, pl. נִדְבָּכִין v 4.
